destination.description: The renderer writes one file. The installer is responsible for copying or linking it into src/resources and /etc.

system.description: Defaults used only when neither CLI nor defaults files provide exact paths.

dev.description: Defaults used only when neither CLI nor defaults files provide exact paths.

managed_variables.name: INSTALL_MODE
managed_variables.description: Selected installation mode used to resolve all mode-dependent paths.

managed_variables.name: MODULES_DIR
managed_variables.description: Modules directory derived from APP_DIR.

managed_variables.name: PLUGINS_DIR
managed_variables.description: Provider plugins directory derived from APP_DIR.

managed_variables.name: BASH_SOURCE
managed_variables.description: In dev mode, allow exported shell variables to override CLI flags and app_env.json values. Ignored in system mode.

managed_variables.name: APP_NAME
managed_variables.description: Stable application identifier used for installation, configuration, state, runtime and systemd names.

managed_variables.name: INSTALL_DIR
managed_variables.description: Absolute directory containing the installed application.

managed_variables.name: APP_DIR
managed_variables.description: Absolute installed application root used to derive module and plugin paths.

managed_variables.name: USER_SYSTEM
managed_variables.description: System account, dev clone account, or invoker selected by plain dev mode.

managed_variables.name: USER_GROUP
managed_variables.description: Resolved group controlling access to installed application files and managed agent configuration.

managed_variables.name: USER_SYSTEM_HOME
managed_variables.source: system passwd database after account resolution
managed_variables.description: Actual home directory of USER_SYSTEM; never construct it solely by concatenating /home and the username.

managed_variables.name: APP_CONFIG_DIR
managed_variables.description: Application-level configuration directory. It is not a location for agent history or messages.

managed_variables.name: APP_DATA_DIR
managed_variables.description: Mutable durable data owned by the application.

managed_variables.name: APP_RUNTIME_DIR
managed_variables.description: Volatile PID and Unix-socket directory.

managed_variables.name: MODULES_MANIFEST_FILE
managed_variables.description: Installed modules manifest filename.

managed_variables.name: MODULES_MANIFEST_PATH
managed_variables.description: Installed modules manifest path derived from APP_CONFIG_DIR.

managed_variables.name: AGENTS_DATA_RUNTIME
managed_variables.description: Unix-socket filename for the dedicated Agents Data runtime.

managed_variables.name: AGENTS_DATA_COMMUNICATION_APP
managed_variables.description: Local HTTP endpoint of the Agents Data communication application.

managed_variables.name: APP_RUNTIME
managed_variables.description: Unix-socket filename for the main application runtime.

managed_variables.name: AGENT_HOME_ROOT
managed_variables.description: Default root for regular agent Linux homes. Actual homes must be confirmed through the passwd database.

managed_variables.name: AGENT_HOME_TEMPLATE
managed_variables.description: Display and planning template only; runtime account lookup remains authoritative.

managed_variables.name: AGENT_RUNTIME_CONFIG_FILE
managed_variables.description: Per-agent runtime configuration, not a PID or socket file.

managed_variables.name: SYSTEM_AGENT_RUNTIME_SOCKET
managed_variables.description: Compatibility alias for APP_RUNTIME_PATH.

managed_variables.name: COMMUNICATION_AGENT_RUNTIME_SOCKET
managed_variables.description: Compatibility alias for AGENTS_DATA_RUNTIME_PATH.

replace_variables.reason: Configuration, durable mutable data and volatile runtime data require different Linux locations.
The target layout stores each agent's configuration in that agent's own Linux home.

steps.description: Parse CLI arguments provided by the user, agent or installer. The shell wrapper resolves its own physical physical application root, invokes exactly src/internal_scripts/render_app_env.py and forwards argv unchanged apart from the package-dir bootstrap value.
Read and validate resources/default_install.json and resources/app_env.template.json as schema_version 1, kind agents-system-environment and an array of uniquely named variables.

Resolve repo values with BASH_SOURCE enabled using environment, flags, app_env.json and defaults in that order; otherwise use flags, app_env.json and defaults; validate APP_NAME, physical application root, INSTALL_DIR, USER_SYSTEM, USER_GROUP and USER_SYSTEM_HOME against the filesystem and passwd database.
For dev mode derive application paths below USER_SYSTEM_HOME; for system mode separate /etc configuration, /var/lib durable data and /run volatile runtime paths.
Build per-agent path templates rooted in the individual agent's home: .agents for config, .history/history.jsonl for activity history and .inbox/communication.json for received messages.
Omit repository checkout, repository metadata and repository history variables; these belong to repo-manager and repo-manifests rather than Agents System environment configuration.
Create the final variables array from the managed-variable contract, resolving nested placeholders deterministically and rejecting unknown, cyclic or unresolved placeholders.
Normalize every absolute path, reject traversal and unexpected symlink escapes, and ensure no history, inbox or mutable runtime path points under /etc.
Verify that config.json, runtime.json, shell.json and shells resolve below /home/{{agent_name}}/.agents, while history and communication resolve to the separate .history and .inbox directories.
Write app_env.json atomically to --output with valid UTF-8 JSON; preserve app_env.template.json unchanged. Refuse to replace an existing output unless --force is present.
Reload the written JSON and verify unique names, fully resolved required values and correct mode-specific paths.
Print or return the rendered output path and resolved-variable names without secrets. Exit codes and output are identical whether invoked by the installer or directly by a user.

ownership_contract.observed_directory_mode: setgid layout requiring explicit policy validation
ownership_contract.note: The existing listing under /home/user-system/.agents/mimir reflects the old central layout and must not be treated as the destination for newly created per-agent configuration. Exact ACL entries are outside this rendering contract and belong to the agent-environment creation service.

failure_policy: Any invalid template, missing required value, duplicate variable name, unresolved or cyclic placeholder, unsafe path or JSON serialization error stops rendering. Write through a temporary sibling file and atomic rename so failure leaves no partial output. Without --force, an existing output is not replaced. No repository-history variable is restored as a fallback.
